newsitem.title: EU: EC Report Weekly Diary for Monday, July 14-Sunday, July 20.
newsitem.headline: EC Report Weekly Diary for Monday, July 14-Sunday, July 20.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
STRASBOURG - European Parliament plenary session (Mon-Fri).
STRASBOURG - European Commission holds weekly meeting (Tues).
STRASBOURG - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner van den Broek hold joint n/conf on EU enlargement (Wed).
BRUSSELS - French President Jacques Chirac meets European Commission President Santer - followed by a joint n/conf (Thurs).
BRUSSELS - First joint NATO-Russia session (Thurs).
BRUSSELS - European Commission and South Africa meet at ministerial level to pursue technical discussions on a bilateral agreement (Fri).
BRUSSELS - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin meets European Commission President Santer and European Commissioner van den Broek - followed by a joint n/conf (Fri).
MONDAY, JULY 14

STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (1700/1500 GMT) (first of five days). Provisional agenda includes presentation by European Ombudsman of 1996 annual report and response by European Commissioner Gradin.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioners Bonino and Fischler attend European Parliament Special Committee of Inquiry into mad cow disease (1800/1600 GMT).
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Luxembourg Education and Culture Minister Erna Hennecot-Schoepges attends European Parliament Culture Committee (1900/1700 GMT).

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "EU enlargement - The industrial consequences" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is: Commission Directorate-General III (Industry) Head Stefano Micossi. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
LUXEMBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker meets Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
TUESDAY, JULY 15

STRASBOURG - European Commission holds weekly meeting (1500/1300 GMT). Agenda includes opinions on EU membership applications of East European countries and "Agenda 2000" proposals on the consequences of enlargement for EU policies in areas including budget, agriculture and aid to poorer members.

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (0900/0700 GMT) (second of five days). Provisional agenda includes debates on legal protection of biotechnological inventions; rules on voice telephony in a competitive environment; conditions under which non-resident carriers may operate national road passenger services within the EU; international transport of passengers by coach or bus; taxation of lorries for use of certain infrastructure; defining a strategy to strengthen air safety.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil Robles holds n/conf on the new agreement on deputies' allowances and openness of parliamentary documents (1200/1000 GMT).
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Austrian Foreign Affairs Secretary of State Benita Ferrero-Waldner meets European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles (1130/0930 GMT).
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - British Minister for Europe Doug Henderson meets European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles (1730/1530 GMT).
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - British Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham attends European Parliament Special Committee of Inquiry into mad cow disease (1730/1530 GMT).

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker addresses European Parliament Employment and Social Affairs Committee on Luxembourg's EU presidency work programme (1730/1530 GMT).
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Luxembourg Energy Minister Robert Goebbels attends European Parliament Research and Energy Committee (1730/1530 GMT).
STRASBOURG - Union for Europe Group President Jean-Claude Pasty holds press lunch (1300/1100 GMT). Venue: Club de la presse, Allee de la Robertsau. Contact: Union for Europe Group (322) 284 1111.
WEDNESDAY, JULY 16

STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (0900/0700 GMT) (third of five days). European Commission presents opinions on EU membership applications of Eastern European countries and "Agenda 2000" proposals on the consequences of enlargement for EU policies in areas including budget, agriculture and aid to poorer members.
Agenda also includes presentation by Luxembourg of its EU presidency programme; statement by the Luxembourg presidency on the incursions by Turkey into northern Iraq.

The parliament will also debate the ARIANE book-translation programme; free movement of doctors and mutual recognition of their diplomas; policy and action on the environment and sustainable development; transfer of waste towards non-OECD member states; partnership accords with Moldova, Ukraine.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner van den Broek hold joint n/conf on "Agenda 2000" proposals on EU enlargement (1200/1000 GMT).

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioners Flynn, Fischler and Wulf-Mathies hold joint n/conf on the consequences of EU enlargement for "structural funds" devoted to poorer regions (1300/1100 GMT), followed by a n/conf by Agriculture Commissioner Fischler on the consequences of enlargement for EU agriculture policy.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Liikanen holds n/conf on the EU's new financial framework (1430/1230 GMT).

BRUSSELS (MODIFIED ITEM) - Fourth International Conference on Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH 4) (to Fri). Regulatory authorities from the European Union, Japan and the United States will discuss scientific and technical aspects of new pharmaceutical product registration. News conference at 1730/1530 GMT. Venue: Palais des Expositions. Contact: Patrick Deboyser, European Commission (322) 295 1529.
THURSDAY, JULY 17
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - French President Jacques Chirac meets European Commission President Santer (1145/0945 GMT) - followed by a joint n/conf at 1430/1230 GMT.

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (1000/0900 GMT) (fourth of five days). Agenda includes votes on topical international questions, including Cambodia, the shutdown of Renault's Vilvoorde plant and anti-personnel mines.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Luxembourg Agriculture Minister Fernand Boden attends Special Committee of Inquiry into mad cow disease (1500/1300 GMT).
BRUSSELS - First joint NATO-Russia session.
FRIDAY, JULY 18

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission and South Africa meet at ministerial level to pursue technical discussions on a future bilateral agreement. Participants include South African Trade Minister Alec Erwin and European Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin meets European Commission President Santer and European Commissioner van den Broek - followed by a joint n/conf at 1300/1100 GMT.

STRASBOURG (MODIFIED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (0900/0700 GMT) (last of five days). Agenda includes votes on financial assistance to Armenia and Georgia and participation of Romania, the Czech Republic and Hungary in EU training and education programmes.
SATURDAY, JULY 19
No events scheduled.
SUNDAY, JULY 20
No events scheduled.
